stem.en: Kabir asks why the cell "does not just have the chain press coins directly, and skip the dam". What does the dam buy?

text.en: Any source of ions counts. Several chains from different carriers all fill one dam, and one kind of turbine drains it. The dam also stores: a few seconds of coins in reserve, and a voltage the cell uses for other things, like pulling pyruvate in.
Nothing; it is a historical accident.

feedback.en: It is old, but it is not pointless. A dam pools many small falls and lets one turbine use all of them.
Nothing adds energy. The dam pools and stores it. The total is set by the electrons' fall.
A chain could in principle be built to press coins. The dam design won because pooling beats point-to-point.

explanation.en: Ajji's pond. Many streams, one wheel. A gradient is a common currency any fall can pay into and any turbine can spend.
